I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I am p3 with $1009 and just won Electric Company for $161. I own Baltic Avenue, Virginia Avenue, and Atlantic Avenue. Player 1 has two orange properties and two red properties but is missing Tennessee and Illinois.

Player 1 also owns Vermont and needs Oriental and Connecticut for a light blue monopoly. Player 2 has St. Charles, Illinois, and Pennsylvania. Player 4 owns Reading Railroad, Connecticut Avenue, Pennsylvania Railroad, and Water Works.

No monopolies are currently held. The pink group is blocked because States and St. Charles are both unowned. Yellow and brown groups look promising since only Ventnor, Marvin, and Mediterranean remain unowned. I am weighing trade, mortgage, or end turn.

Player 1 poses the biggest threat. Completing an orange or red monopoly there would be dangerous. Player 2 correctly refused to trade Illinois to Player 1. I am now weighing whether to propose a trade.

Trading is not worthwhile right now. I cannot offer a complete color set yet, and the pieces I need are mostly unowned. Acquiring Water Works from Player 4 would not be strong enough to justify a deal, and Player 4 recently refused to pay more than $160 for Electric Company. My cash position of $1009 is solid enough to wait.

I am now considering trading for Illinois from Player 2 to block Player 1's red monopoly. Player 2 previously rejected a deal for it, so they may demand a high price. I am weighing whether to offer Virginia Avenue in exchange, though that would give Player 2 two pink properties and leave me without my pink foothold.

I rejected trading Virginia or Atlantic for Illinois because that would create a future pink monopoly threat. I also dismissed Electric Company and cash as poor offers. I am now looking for a trade with Player 2 that blocks Player 1 without giving Player 2 a monopoly.

Player 2 cannot trade Illinois to Player 1 because Player 1 already owns two red properties. Player 2 also needs two more greens to complete that set. I will end my turn.

I am now considering trading Virginia Avenue for St. Charles Place from Player 2. That would give me two of three pink properties and leave only States unowned. Player 2 recently bought St. Charles for $140, so they may not sell it immediately. I am weighing an offer of $200 to $250.

Player 2 likely wants more than cash for St. Charles since they just acquired it. Trading Virginia for St. Charles would be pointless because I would still only have one pink property. I rejected offering Electric Company plus cash for St. Charles because Player 2 recently bought it and would reject the deal.

Player 1 can complete an orange monopoly by landing on the unowned Tennessee Avenue for $180, which is the most immediate threat. Player 4 owns two railroads and two unowned railroads remain. I am now looking for a trade with Player 2 or Player 4 that is clearly beneficial.

A railroad monopoly is strong but slow. I will end my turn. No trade is clearly profitable right now. Proposing a bad deal would waste a message and signal desperation. Player 2 already refused to trade Illinois to Player 1.
